tickets.title: Third Avenue L stop closure pilot proposal
tickets.summary: Speaker Joshua Wul said his simulation using MTA trip data found that only about 5% of riders board or exit at the Third Avenue L stop, so closing it would save New Yorkers roughly 1,800 hours daily. He noted the stop is not a transfer station and is not wheelchair accessible. Action: Refer the Third Avenue stop closure proposal to the transportation committee and ask the MTA about a pilot closure.

tickets.title: E-bike storage and obstruction at 11th Street
tickets.summary: Over 100 electric delivery bikes are stored on the sidewalk and street at 11th Street and First Avenue, obstructing businesses and residents and raising fire concerns. The precinct plans enforcement and bike confiscation starting October 7, while the delivery workers face hardship, and the district office notes that legal parking and corral space is lacking. Speakers asked for translated warnings and a delay in enforcement in favor of tagging the bikes. Action: Coordinate with the precinct, sanitation, and the council office on enforcement notice in multiple languages and on finding legal parking or corral sites for the bikes.

tickets.title: Drug activity and lighting in Seward Park
tickets.summary: Residents and the Seward Park Conservancy report increased drug use and homelessness in Seward Park, including near a bathroom beside the Lower East Side Ecology Center. A speaker noted dark spots with poor lighting that may enable drug use, and asked whether mobile crisis teams could be used instead of police. The district manager said police are stationed there under a task force and outreach providers are active. Action: Ask the precinct and Parks to sustain police presence, repair out-of-service lights through 311, and assess expanding mobile crisis response.

tickets.title: 11 Allen Street liquor license recommendation denial
tickets.summary: The SLA August agenda item for 11 Allen Street, tied to an operator formerly at Time Cafe on Forsyth and Canal, was debated over stipulations for a full liquor license in an unlicensed location near Dime Square. The board voted 20 to 10 with nine abstentions to recommend outright denial, but residents noted that without community attendance at the SLA hearing, the permit could be granted without stipulations. Action: Organize residents to attend the SLA hearing to support the denial and have elected officials advised, and ask staff to watch the SLA calendar and add context on past complaints.

tickets.title: Correct August SLA resolutions for two locations
tickets.summary: The board chair reported clerical errors in two August SLA resolutions. Item 10, Soft Hours Tea House, should read a recommended denial of a beer and wine license unless stipulations are agreed to, not a full on-premises license, and item 3, Cozy Cafe, should likewise read a beer and wine license denial. Action: Correct the resolution text for Soft Hours Tea House and Cozy Cafe before the resolutions are transmitted to the SLA.

tickets.title: Essex Market RFP timing and content
tickets.summary: The joint land use and economic development committee met with EDC about the Essex Market request for proposals, which was due to go out by the end of the month. EDC could not confirm that the board's two prior resolutions for a community market were incorporated. The committee asked EDC to postpone issuing the RFP. Action: Meet with EDC later this week to clarify how the resolutions were addressed and press for postponing the RFP issuance.

tickets.title: Public restroom pilot access and operations
tickets.summary: The city is installing 17 free public restrooms citywide as a one-year pilot, with two in the district, including one near Delancey Plaza and one at Cooper Square and East Sixth Street. Concerns were raised about access rules, who can use them, and emergency calls. DOT will lead installation in mid-October. Action: Prepare a resolution for next month's meeting setting out access and emergency procedures for the restroom pilot period.

tickets.title: Manhattan Bridge exits and Canal Street redesign
tickets.summary: The transportation committee sent a letter to the mayor and DOT reiterating community concerns about the Manhattan Bridge exits, especially after a recent fatal crash. The letter also asked for an update on the Canal Street redesign, as the board has had no update since January. Action: Follow up with DOT and the mayor's office for a response to the letter and an update on the Canal Street redesign.

tickets.title: Congestion pricing impact on FDR Drive
tickets.summary: A committee member asked whether projected congestion increases on the FDR from congestion pricing, noted in the air quality report and an earlier board resolution, actually occurred. The member asked whether MTA or DOT would return to discuss it. Action: Request reporting from MTA and DOT on actual FDR congestion impacts and any planned follow-up.

tickets.title: District housing plan affordability shortfall
tickets.summary: The city's draft housing plan proposes about 7,000 units in five years for the district, but roughly 75% are market rate, which falls short of the board's top priority for affordable housing. The board submitted comments on a short turnaround based on the district needs statement. Members asked for ongoing opportunities to weigh in, noting shrinking comment windows. Action: Have land use committees take positions on future housing plans proactively rather than waiting for short comment periods.

tickets.title: October vote on district needs and budget priorities
tickets.summary: The board will vote in October on its district needs statement and ranked expense and capital budget priorities for city agencies. District managers are meeting with over 20 agencies to learn about cuts, vacancies, and funding gaps before the vote. Ranking will be done within each agency, with examples such as summer youth employment. Action: Have each committee develop and rank expense and capital priorities for its agencies ahead of the October full board vote.

tickets.title: Support mobile voting for school council elections
tickets.summary: The education committee brought a resolution supporting a pilot mobile voting option for community education council elections, since turnout has been about 2% and many households rely only on smartphones. Speakers asked that outreach clarify eligibility, that privacy and immigration concerns be addressed, and that the vote be framed as school participation. The resolution was modeled on CEC1 guidance. Action: Send the resolution to the Department of Education's family and community empowerment office urging a mobile-first pilot and expanded multilingual outreach.

tickets.title: Proposed bylaws changes on attendance removal
tickets.summary: The bylaws committee presented proposed changes that would replace automatic removal for missed meetings with an early letter and a meeting with the executive committee after too many absences. The changes would also remove attendance from the general removal process and require public members to follow conflict of interest policies. Members questioned the double recommendation step, and the chair said the process is not punitive. Action: Vote on the proposed bylaws changes at the October full board meeting, with the 28-day notice sent out in advance.

tickets.title: Board trainings on SLA and Robert's Rules
tickets.summary: The board chair announced plans for trainings on SLA procedures, Robert's Rules, and office procedures, mainly to help new members and refresh others. Dates have not been set. The chair also noted that members often talk among themselves rather than asking questions. Action: Schedule the SLA, Robert's Rules, and office procedures trainings and have members email the chair with requested training topics.

tickets.title: NYCHA residents need food and communication access
tickets.summary: A public speaker described long-term hardship for NYCHA residents, including lack of food, water, necessities, and work, and asked how families will get basic supplies. A deaf and hard-of-hearing speaker said communication access is essential and asked that the community address drugs and toxicity. Action: Refer the NYCHA food, necessities, and communication access concerns to the appropriate city agencies and social service providers.

tickets.title: Proposed indoor roller skating facility on East River Pier
tickets.location_raw: East River Pier across from the Katherine Slip Mall
tickets.summary: A speaker proposed a 300,000 square foot multi-use building with indoor roller skating on an East River pier, with admission set at $8 including skate rentals. The speaker projected 250 to 400 direct jobs and said the site is between the Manhattan and Brooklyn Bridges. Action: Refer the pier roller skating proposal to the land use committee for review of site use and community input.

tickets.title: MetroCard help for immigrant center visitors
tickets.summary: A speaker asked whether MetroCards or other transit support would be available for immigrants traveling to the new Manhattan Immigrant Welcome Center on 125th Street, since the trip can take an hour with transfers. The speaker also asked whether downtown organizations could partner with the center. The district office said it would raise the transit question with the liaison. Action: Raise the transit cost assistance question with the elected official's office and report back to the board.
